2609.04453.title: When Load-Balancing Goes Too Far: Expert Pruning in Over-Dispersed Mixture-of-Experts Models
2609.04453.paper_summary: Expert pruning reduces the memory and serving cost of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by removing low-importance experts identified by the router, assuming router probabilities provide a reliable importance signal. We observe that this assumption breaks down under over-dispersed routing, a regime associated with aggressive load-balancing during training, in which tokens are distributed nearly uniformly across experts and importance signals collapse. In this regime, perplexity does not predict downstream task accuracy: on gpt-oss-20B, the lowest-perplexity pruning configuration yields the worst mathematical reasoning, while the highest-perplexity configuration preserves it. This does not occur under standard routing (e.g., Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct), where perplexity and accuracy degrade together. Pruning under over-dispersed routing also exposes a capability trade-off in which no single scoring metric dominates: activation-aware scoring preserves mathematical reasoning but severely degrades knowledge-intensive science (an 18-point gap on GPQA), whereas frequency-based scoring exhibits the reverse. We propose Minimax Expert Score Allocation (MESA), a domain-aware method that iteratively boosts importance scores for experts serving whichever domain is currently worst-affected, minimizing worst-case domain degradation rather than average accuracy. At 25% expert pruning MESA achieves the smallest worst-case degradation across domains, outperforming activation-aware baselines on 7 of 11 benchmarks at a correspondingly reduced memory footprint, and it generalizes to gpt-oss-120B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B, and OLMoE-1B-7B. Our results indicate that over-dispersed routing is a qualitatively distinct pruning regime in which standard assumptions fail, and that recognizing it is a prerequisite for principled expert pruning of load-balanced MoE models.
2609.04453.paper_summary_zh: 專家修剪透過移除路由器識別的低重要性專家，降低混合專家（MoE）模型的記憶體和服務成本，假設路由器概率提供可靠的重要性信號。<lb/>我們觀察到，在過度分散的路由下，這一假設失效，這種情況與訓練期間的激進負載平衡相關，令令牌幾乎均勻地分配到各專家之間，並且重要性信號崩潰。<lb/>在這種情況下，困惑度無法預測下游任務的準確性：在 gpt-oss-20B 上，最低困惑度的修剪配置產生了最差的數學推理，而最高困惑度的配置則保留了這一能力。<lb/>在標準路由（例如，Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct）下並不會發生這種情況，困惑度和準確性會一起下降。<lb/>在過度分散的路由下的修剪也暴露出一種能力權衡，沒有單一的評分指標佔主導地位：基於激活的評分保留了數學推理，但嚴重削弱了知識密集型科學（在 GPQA 上有 18 分的差距），而基於頻率的評分則呈現相反的情況。<lb/>我們提出了最小化專家評分分配（MESA），這是一種領域感知的方法，通過迭代提升對當前受影響最嚴重的領域的專家的重要性分數，最小化最壞情況的領域退化，而不是平均準確性。<lb/>在 25% 專家修剪下，MESA 在各領域中實現了最小的最壞情況退化，在 11 個基準中有 7 個超越了基於激活的基準，並且相應地減少了記憶體佔用，並且它可以推廣到 gpt-oss-120B、Gemma-4-26B-A4B 和 OLMoE-1B-7B。<lb/>我們的結果表明，過度分散的路由是一種質量上不同的修剪模式，其中標準假設失效，而認識到這一點是對負載平衡的 MoE 模型進行原則性專家修剪的前提。
